explanation: Fires on an abstract or general head noun that comes right after 'the' (or a similar determiner) and is usually followed by an 'of'-phrase or other modifier, e.g. 'the [period] of', 'the [time] of', 'the [findings] of', 'any [questions] you may have'. The token must be a noun in a determiner + noun + complement frame; concrete nouns or nouns without a following complement give weak activation.

Fires on tokens in the middle of identifiers: digits inside long ID numbers (DOI/URL item IDs, comment IDs), and subword or suffix pieces of code identifiers and compound words (e.g. '$[method]', 'Header[Class]', 'virtual[ization]'). It also fires sporadically on ordinary prose words, so the pattern is loose.

Fires on the token right before a number or argument in formulaic/code text: the space before a number ('picking [ ]2', 'age of [ ]21', 'Standard [ ]2.0'), 'on [an] "AS IS"' in license boilerplate, and code tokens right before an argument such as 'rotate', 'fadeOut(' and 'Set-Location'. In short, a slot directly before a predictable value in templated text.

Fires on a finite verb or auxiliary (was, am, can, is, are, would, will, don't) that starts a second predicate whose subject is left out, usually right after 'but' or 'and' ('X, but [was] given...', 'I'm using Y and [am] running'). It also fires, more weakly, on a verb right after a complex subject phrase. Auxiliaries with an explicit pronoun subject right before them give weak activation.

Mixed: fires on tokens in license/copyright boilerplate ('the Corporation [nor]', 'names [of]', 'may be [reproduced]'), on code tokens such as parameter names, class keywords and identifier pieces, on math symbols, and on scattered prose words. No common thread is visible.

Fires on a token right after a subject noun phrase or modal, typically a verb, auxiliary or preposition that starts the predicate ('includes but [is]', 'that [can] result', 'may [appear]', 'will generally [be]', 'previously [in]'). It also fires on odd items such as drug-name suffixes and prices. Strongest in scientific or formal prose.

Fires on miscellaneous tokens in technical text: the second item in argument lists or macros (sd3(x[,y]...)), command-line placeholders, shell redirects, and boilerplate words in licenses and legal citations ('et [al]', 'software and [associated]'), plus some news-prose nouns. No single theme.

Fires on the first or a middle subword piece of a word the tokenizer splits up, especially proper names, foreign words and Cyrillic text ('пр[ив]ет', 'R[ix]ensart', 'Xe[La]TeX', '[DEN]IES', '[Pri]yanka', '[Per]vez'). Common whole-word tokens give little activation.

Fires on tokens inside alphanumeric codes and names that are split into pieces: digits in error codes and model numbers ('C[2]061', 'S[7]-300', hex colors), syllables in the middle of foreign or proper names ('T[enz]ing', 'Udz[ung]wa'), plus fixed license-boilerplate words ('OF [ANY] KIND', 'Use of this [software]').

Fires mainly on the token 'head' (HTML '<head>', 'Head'teacher, 'head'ache, 'heady') and on a middle subword piece of 'electro-' words ('elect[ros]pray', 'electr[r]ification'), plus a few other split subwords ('Ab[aba]', 'far[c]ical'). Ordinary words give weak activation.

Fires on 'of' directly after purpose/aim/goal nouns, especially in 'The purpose of this study was to', 'The aim of', 'The goal of'. Weaker on similar function words after framing nouns ('wrong [with]', 'Here['s]'); 'of' in other contexts is near zero.
Fires almost only on a '0' digit inside long runs of zeros (e.g. '000000[0]0'). Everything else (import 'from', 'android[:]', 'using [System]') stays at or below about 12%.

Fires on the verb or complement token right after a negated or impossibility modal: 'cannot [be]', 'can't [be]', 'could not [be]', 'has never [been]', 'impossible [to]', 'difficult [to]', 'can['t]'. Positive 'can [be]' and other contexts are much weaker.

One extreme top example (a column-header abbreviation, 'Sth[Am]', in a text table). The rest are weak (about 30% or less): tokens inside code, tables and file headers, such as variable names, docblock tags and timestamp digits. The function is unclear beyond formatted, table-like or code text.
